findings.evidence: “Set up (or refresh) ai-kit's cross-AI lanes: the review and execute lanes and each role's order, written to the [lanes] table of config.toml” repeats the already-loaded description without adding a decision or constraint.
findings.fix: Record the removal of this duplicate restatement; keep the next lines that route the agent to the config reference and set the workflow order.

findings.evidence: “Skip this section unless a preferred runtime has no listing” is encountered in Step 1.5, before wizard-flow step 1 asks for preferred runtimes. The later listing-less branch does not route back to this section, so a first-time Copilot setup can miss the documented discovery options.
findings.fix: Keep the initial catalog build in Step 1.5. After the owner selects preferred runtimes, route each selected listing-less runtime to the optional discovery section before proposing lanes. Preserve the separate consent gate for launching a herdr pane.

findings.evidence: The main file is 418 lines but contains about 6,400 words. The always-loaded body includes the full check-reviewer command and its detailed argument, output and error handling even for requests that stop at detection.
findings.fix: Keep the write-risk gate and test outcomes in Step 2.5. Move the exact invocation, argument rules and usability response details to a dedicated reference loaded only when testing a selected pair.

findings.evidence: “Build the catalog from the whole snapshot: see catalog.md § Build and classify” sends readers back through a third document after SKILL.md routes them to wizard-flow.md and the wizard routes them here.
findings.fix: Put the shared catalog-build instructions in catalog.md alone and route to them directly from SKILL.md at the detection and selected-runtime refresh checkpoints. Keep selection-specific candidate and confirmation instructions in cli-model-selection.md.

findings.evidence: “A change made between that read and the write is not caught.” Replacement consent is tied to a particular roster, but --replace is not tied to the version the owner approved; a concurrent edit can still be overwritten.
findings.fix: Have render-toml accept an expected roster digest, check it under the existing writer lock before migration or replacement, and refuse on mismatch. Pass the digest from the approval step and re-ask on refusal.

findings.evidence: “Just check which reviewers are available, and do not change anything” has no roster fixture or scripted answer, but its assertions cover both all-read-only and unconfirmed-write-risk profiles as well as probe approval and refusal. A single run cannot exercise all those outcomes.
findings.fix: Split the check-only eval into an all-read-only approval case and an unconfirmed-risk refusal case. Supply a roster and profile fixture for each, script the owner's answer, and assert the exact probe calls and reported availability.

findings.evidence: “ai-kit-spec-review keeps telling me no lanes exist” covers the review handoff, but the suite's execute prompts do not exercise the corresponding no-roster handoff from the superpowers adapter.
findings.fix: Replace two overlapping positive queries with one in which the execute adapter offers setup because no execute lanes exist. Keep the existing already-configured execute request as the paired negative.

findings.evidence: The preflight serializes entry fields only when “'command' in by_key[k]”. A table-runtime lane can change effort, tier or mode after consent without changing the compared JSON, so the approved list can match even though the probe invocation changed.
findings.fix: Include every effective setting that affects quota-probe invocation in the preview and in the recheck, preferably through a shared read-only preflight used by probe-quota itself. Re-ask whenever those settings differ.

findings.evidence: “An added lane counts as the fallback only once it is kept through those steps and is not usage-limited itself” does not recheck the pool when the owner names a different candidate. An unflagged free candidate in the same pool still cannot be a fallback.
findings.fix: After validating an added or owner-named candidate, reapply the full fallback rule: it must be selectable for the role, unflagged, and outside the original lane's pool. Otherwise ask for another candidate or an explicit none.

findings.evidence: “A custom entry never runs as an executor” is stated after the test instruction, and the branch offers a replacement without explicitly removing the ineligible lane. The wizard can test a command that cannot serve the requested role and then carry it into the execute order.
findings.fix: Before testing or building either role's order, remove a custom command from the execute set and confirm a supported table-runtime or session-default replacement, or leave execute empty. If it was also approved for review, retain and test it for review only.
